title: India's engineering exports climb 21% to $11.48 bn as China demand surges 74%
summary: India's engineering exports rose 21% year-on-year to $11.48 billion in June, driven by a 74% jump in demand from China and strong orders from the US, Germany and Oman. Engineering shipments grew 18.09% in the April–June quarter, supporting overall merchandise exports despite higher logistics costs and shipping disruptions.
content:
India's engineering exports rose 21% year-on-year to $11.48 billion in June, supported by strong demand from China, the US, Germany and Oman despite shipping disruptions in the Red Sea and Strait of Hormuz. The headline increase included a notable 74% surge in shipments to China, reflecting buoyant external demand for capital goods and intermediate components.

Engineering exports grew 18.09% in the April-June quarter, helping support India's merchandise exports amid rising logistics costs. Exporters faced higher freight rates and longer transit times as vessels rerouted to avoid high-risk zones, yet continued orders from major markets helped offset these headwinds.

The performance highlights resilience in India's manufacturing and engineering sectors and the benefits of diversified export markets. Analysts note that while elevated shipping expenses and geopolitical risks pose short-term challenges, robust overseas demand — particularly from China and Western markets — has sustained shipment volumes.

Industry bodies and policymakers are monitoring developments in key shipping lanes and encouraging further value addition, quality upgrades and market diversification to sustain momentum. Continued gains in engineering exports will be important for India’s broader export recovery and for supporting domestic manufacturing growth.
